STEP 1 - Scene: A single white plate holding a mound of soft, crumbly white cheese (looks like fresh curd or feta-style cheese, with some creamy pieces). Photographed from above, roughly top-down. Other plates at the left edge (fried/roasted brown pieces, possibly potatoes or meat) are not part of this plate.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish white plate, about 26 cm across its width. Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2 (treating it as roughly round for the estimate; the square plate is similar in area).

STEP 3 - Items: One food: white crumbly/soft cheese (curd-style cheese). No visible sauce or oil.

STEP 4 - Area: The cheese covers roughly 30% of the plate (about 160 cm^2), a compact mound in the center-right.

STEP 5 - Volume: Mound height averages about 2 cm (some pieces are taller). 160 cm^2 x 2 cm ≈ 320 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cheese bulk density ~0.9 g/ml. 320 ml x 0.9 ≈ 290 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Fresh crumbly white cheese (feta-style) ≈ 265 kcal/100 g. 290 g x 2.65 ≈ 770 kcal. Note: if it is a lower-fat fresh curd (~100–150 kcal/100 g), energy would be far lower; feta-style is assumed here given the crumbly texture and salty look.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A ~290 g mound of cheese on a dinner plate is plausible for a large portion. Energy is high but consistent with the density of cheese. Estimate is uncertain by roughly ±40%.
